title: Reading a generative-AI paper in 20 minutes

questions.q: A paper says 'better than the state of the art' with no setting listed. What's missing?
options: The baseline at the same settings, and the measure
questions.answer: The baseline at the same settings, and the measure
questions.why: You need to know better than what, by which number, on what data.

questions.q: A method's best of 30 runs beats the baseline's mean by 2 run-noise units, with no true gain. Why?
options: Taking the maximum of many noisy runs inflates the number
questions.answer: Taking the maximum of many noisy runs inflates the number
questions.why: The lab reaches about 2.04 with a true gain of 0.

questions.q: No spread is reported. What should you conclude?
options: You can't judge whether the difference is real
questions.answer: You can't judge whether the difference is real
questions.why: The last row of the second table: no spread, no judgement.

questions.q: A paper reports eight metrics and wins on one by a clear margin. How should you read that?
options: With care: one of many can favour it by chance
As proof of a real gain
It means the other seven are wrong
questions.answer: With care: one of many can favour it by chance
questions.why: The lab's chance of one clear win with no real difference is 32%.

questions.q: A paper gets lower error at 20 steps by calling the model twice per step. What fair comparison should you ask for?
questions.why: Steps hide cost. See heun in CU-470.
